nodes.content: Enable cross-lingual morphological inflection transfer to low-resource languages with grammatical feature combinations absent from source languages.
requirements: Use at most 200 labeled inflections per target language; evaluate on unseen lemmas.
Exceed matched-budget multilingual fine-tuning exact-match accuracy by five percentage points on source-absent feature combinations.

nodes.content: Train a factorized character transducer on source paradigms; compose absent feature bundles and fit target morphotactic adapters on 200 forms.
Can 200-form target adapters resolve nonconcatenative allomorphy for source-absent feature bundles on unseen lemmas?
Morphotactic adapters learn nonconcatenative allomorphy from 200 forms, improving unseen-lemma exact-match ≥5 points over matched-budget fine-tuning on source-absent bundles.
Build UniMorph 4.0 source-absent bundle splits; train 200-form adapters and matched-budget baselines; compare unseen-lemma exact-match and nonconcatenative errors.
Run five-seed UniMorph 4.0 Arabic and Maltese target splits using 200 labels; compare unseen-lemma source-absent-bundle exact-match against matched-budget multilingual fine-tuning.
With 200 labels, Arabic/Maltese nonconcatenative source-absent bundles reached 52.4% unseen-lemma exact-match versus 45.8% matched-budget fine-tuning, averaged over five seeds.
Advance factorized adapters to broader-language testing: Arabic/Maltese source-absent exact-match exceeded matched-budget fine-tuning by 6.6 points.
Test 200-form adapters against matched-budget fine-tuning on Turkish, Finnish, and Georgian unseen lemmas, stratified by source-absent bundles.
Run five-seed UniMorph 4.0 Turkish, Finnish, and Georgian splits; score unseen-lemma source-absent-bundle exact-match against matched-budget multilingual fine-tuning.
UniMorph 4.0 benchmark: Turkish, Finnish, and Georgian source-absent-bundle splits, five-seed unseen-lemma exact-match tables, and matched-budget 200-label training scripts.
Audit benchmark splits for lemma leakage and source-bundle overlap; reproduce five-seed exact-match tables with its 200-label scripts.
Audit found zero lemma leakage or source-bundle overlap; adapters gained 6.1 unseen-lemma exact-match points over matched-budget fine-tuning.
Disabling feature-conditioned stem-edit templates reduces Arabic/Maltese unseen-lemma exact-match by ≥4 points on source-absent nonconcatenative bundles.
Ablate feature-conditioned stem-edit templates on five-seed Arabic/Maltese 200-label splits, retaining parameter-matched adapters; measure source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match.
On five-seed Arabic/Maltese splits, removing stem-edit templates reduced source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match from 52.4% to 50.9%, only 1.5 points.
Replicate the 200-label Arabic/Maltese stem-template ablation on root-and-pattern verbs, reporting source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match by vowel-change class.
On root-and-pattern verbs, templates raised source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match from 43.2% to 48.1%, a 4.9-point gain.
Does template utility depend on root-and-pattern prevalence, explaining the 4.9-point verb gain versus 1.5-point aggregate gain?
Estimate five-seed template-ablation gains across Arabic/Maltese root-and-pattern prevalence bins, comparing the 1.5-point aggregate and 4.9-point verb effects.
Induce paradigm classes from unlabeled target text; anchor slots with 200 labeled forms and infer unseen-lemma source-absent bundles analogically.
Mine target-corpus edit-pattern neighborhoods, anchor 200 labeled forms, and benchmark source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match against matched-budget multilingual fine-tuning.
Cluster target-corpus wordforms by shared edit patterns and align clusters to paradigm slots using 200 UniMorph 4.0 labels.
ParadigmAtlas v1: target-corpus edit-pattern clusters, 200-label slot alignments, and analogy candidates for unseen lemmas with source-absent bundles.
Run five-seed Turkish/Finnish/Georgian unseen-lemma tests using ParadigmAtlas v1; report source-absent-bundle candidate coverage and exact-match versus matched-budget multilingual fine-tuning.
ParadigmAtlas v1 achieved 84% gold-candidate coverage and 57.0% unseen-lemma exact-match versus 50.8% matched-budget fine-tuning on source-absent bundles across Turkish/Finnish/Georgian.
Pretrain a multilingual lemma–form cycle model; adapt with unlabeled target wordforms and 200 anchors to compose source-absent feature bundles.
Can cycle consistency and 200 anchors assign feature slots to unlabeled target forms without collapsing source-absent bundles?
With 200 anchors, cycle consistency achieves ≥80% target slot accuracy and ≤10% erroneous source-absent bundle collapse on unseen lemmas.
Audit five-seed Turkish/Finnish/Georgian 200-anchor cycle models for unseen-lemma slot accuracy and erroneous source-absent-bundle collapse.
Five-seed Turkish/Finnish/Georgian audit found 74% unseen-lemma slot accuracy and 17% erroneous source-absent-bundle collapse, missing both thresholds.
Run five-seed Arabic/Maltese 200-anchor cycle-model audits, measuring unseen-lemma slot accuracy and source-absent-bundle collapse against 80%/10% thresholds.
Arabic/Maltese five-seed cycle models reached 83% unseen-lemma slot accuracy and 8% source-absent-bundle collapse with 200 anchors.
Does target-corpus paradigm ambiguity explain why cycle models meet slot-alignment thresholds in Arabic/Maltese but fail in Turkish/Finnish/Georgian?
Estimate target-corpus paradigm ambiguity per language, then regress five-seed slot accuracy and bundle collapse on ambiguity and corpus size.
Compute candidate-slot entropy in five target corpora; regress audited slot accuracy and bundle-collapse rates on entropy, controlling corpus size.
AmbiguityAudit v1: five-language candidate-slot entropy tables, corpus-size-adjusted regressions for slot accuracy and bundle collapse, and reproducible scripts.
Pretrain a feature-compositional transducer on counterfactual bundle swaps, then calibrate target phonotactic constraints with 200 labeled inflections.
Do counterfactual bundle swaps teach valid feature composition, or bias target calibration toward unattested phonotactics?
Counterfactual swaps improve source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match ≥5 points over matched-budget fine-tuning, with ≤5% phonotactic violations after 200-label calibration.
Ablate counterfactual swaps across five targets; compare 200-label source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match and phonotactic violations against matched-budget fine-tuning.
Run five-seed swap ablations across five 200-label targets; compare source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match and phonotactic violations against matched-budget fine-tuning.
Across five targets, swaps reached 59.1% source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match (no-swaps: 54.5%; fine-tuning: 52.8%) with 3.6% phonotactic violations.
Audit per-language five-seed gains and phonotactic violation rates at 200 labels, stratifying source-absent bundles by counterfactual edit distance.
Expanded phonotactic audit uncovered omitted vowel-harmony constraints; five-target violation rate rose from 3.6% to 6.4%, exceeding 5%.
Can vowel-harmony-aware filtering reduce audited violations below 5% without erasing the 6.3-point exact-match advantage?
Adding 200-label vowel-harmony filters to swap decoding yields <5% audited violations and ≥5-point source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match gains over fine-tuning.
Fit vowel-harmony filters using existing 200-label splits, rerun five-target swap decoding, and compare audited violations and exact-match with prior results.
Run five-seed filtered/unfiltered swap decoding on five 200-label targets; measure audited violations and source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match versus fine-tuning.
Penalty-calibrated swaps gained 5.3 exact-match points with 4.8% audited violations; vowel-harmony filters gained only 4.1 despite 3.2% violations.
Cross-validate soft harmony penalties within existing 200-label splits; test per-language ≥5-point exact-match gains and <5% audited violations.
Sweep soft harmony penalties across five targets, selecting by cross-validation within 200 labels; score held-out unseen-lemma exact-match and audited violations.
Cross-validated soft harmony filtering gained 5.2 points in source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match, with 4.6% audited violations across five targets.
Adopt cross-validated soft harmony filtering: it retains a 5.2-point exact-match gain with fewer violations than penalty-calibrated swaps (4.6% versus 4.8%).
Test soft-filtered swaps on Hungarian and Estonian source-absent bundles using 200 labels; require ≥5-point unseen-lemma exact-match gains over matched-budget fine-tuning.
Run five-seed Hungarian/Estonian UniMorph 4.0 unseen-lemma splits with 200-label soft-filtered swaps; score source-absent-bundle exact-match versus matched-budget fine-tuning.
HarmonyTransfer v1: Hungarian/Estonian 200-label splits, soft-filtered swap checkpoints, five-seed source-absent-bundle exact-match tables, and matched-budget baseline scripts.
Audit HarmonyTransfer v1 for lemma leakage; reproduce five-seed Hungarian/Estonian source-absent-bundle exact-match gains and phonotactic violations using 200 labels.
Audit confirmed zero lemma leakage; Hungarian/Estonian source-absent-bundle unseen-lemma exact-match gains were 5.7/5.3 points, with 4.2% phonotactic violations.
